understandable: I will go to the company.
natural: I'm heading to the office.
alts: I go to the enterprise.
I will go to the firm.
why: Use 'the office' for your workplace and the present continuous for plans already arranged.

understandable: I have 10 years working here.
natural: I've been working here for 10 years.
alts: I am working here since 10 years.
I work here from 10 years.
why: Use the present perfect continuous with 'for' + a period of time for something that started in the past and continues now.

pt: Eu fiz uma viagem para o Rio.
understandable: I made a travel to Rio.
natural: I took a trip to Rio.
alts: I did a travel to Rio.
I took a travel to Rio.
why: 'Travel' is mostly uncountable (verb or general idea). For a single journey use 'trip' with 'take'.

understandable: They gonna miss the flight.
natural: They're going to miss the flight.
alts: They going to miss the flight.
They will to miss the flight.
why: 'Gonna' is spoken shorthand for 'going to', but the verb 'are' still has to be there: 'They're gonna...' or 'They're going to...'.

understandable: I am agree with you.
natural: I agree with you.
alts: I'm in agree with you.
I agree to you.
why: 'Agree' is already a verb in English, so you don't use 'be'. The preposition is 'with' for a person.

understandable: What hour is it?
natural: What time is it?
alts: Which hour is it?
How much time is it?
why: In English we ask 'What time is it?'. 'Hour' is used for a duration (an hour) rather than clock time.

understandable: I live here since 2019.
natural: I've lived here since 2019.
alts: I am living here since 2019.
I live here from 2019.
why: 'Since' needs a perfect tense (present perfect) when the situation started in the past and continues now.

understandable: I have hunger.
natural: I'm hungry.
alts: I am with hunger.
I have much hunger.
why: In English, hunger and thirst use 'be' + adjective: 'I'm hungry', 'I'm thirsty'.

pt: Você pode me emprestar sua caneta?
understandable: Can you borrow me your pen?
natural: Could you lend me your pen?
alts: Can I lend your pen?
Could you borrow your pen to me?
why: You lend something TO someone and borrow something FROM someone. 'Could' sounds more polite than 'can'.

pt: Eu tenho uma reunião às 3 horas.
understandable: I have a meeting in the 3 o'clock.
natural: I have a meeting at 3.
alts: I have a meeting on 3 o'clock.
I have a meeting to 3 o'clock.
why: Use 'at' for clock times: at 3, at noon, at 9:30.

understandable: I have 30 years.
natural: I'm 30 years old.
alts: I am with 30 years.
I have 30 years old.
why: English uses 'be' for age, not 'have'. You can also just say 'I'm 30'.

understandable: I arrived in home late.
natural: I got home late.
alts: I arrived to home late.
I reached to home late.
why: 'Home' works as an adverb, so there's no preposition: 'get home', 'go home', 'come home'.

pt: Eu me dou bem com meu chefe.
understandable: I give well with my boss.
natural: I get along well with my boss.
alts: I give me well with my boss.
I go well with my boss.
why: 'Get along (well) with' someone means to have a good relationship with them.

understandable: My computer stopped.
natural: My computer froze.
alts: My computer hanged.
My computer is stuck up.
why: A computer that stops responding 'freezes' (or 'crashes' if it shuts down). 'Hanged' is only used for executions; 'hung' exists for computers, but 'froze' is the everyday word.

understandable: Can you send me the archive?
natural: Can you send me the file?
alts: Can you send the file for me?
Can you send me the archive document?
why: 'Archive' means a long-term collection of records. A computer 'arquivo' is a 'file'. Also, send something TO someone, not 'for' someone.

pt: Estou esperando você há uma hora.
understandable: I am waiting for you since one hour.
natural: I've been waiting for you for an hour.
alts: I wait for you since one hour.
I am waiting you for one hour ago.
why: Use the present perfect continuous with 'for' + duration. 'Ago' never goes with the perfect tenses.

pt: Eu te dou um retorno amanhã.
understandable: I will give you a return tomorrow.
natural: I'll get back to you tomorrow.
alts: I will return you tomorrow.
I'll give you a feedback tomorrow.
why: 'Get back to someone' means to reply later. 'Feedback' is uncountable, and 'return' doesn't mean 'resposta'.

understandable: I have nostalgia of you.
natural: I miss you.
alts: I am with missing of you.
I feel nostalgia for you.
why: 'Miss' is a transitive verb covering 'sentir saudade'. 'Nostalgia' is for the past in general, not a person.

understandable: I think that yes.
natural: I think so.
alts: I think yes.
I think it yes.
why: Use 'so' to replace a whole clause after verbs like think, hope, guess: 'I think so', 'I hope so'. Negative: 'I don't think so'.

understandable: I work with IT.
natural: I work in IT.
alts: I work on IT.
I work at IT.
why: Use 'in' for a field or industry: in IT, in finance, in marketing.

understandable: Enter in the link.
natural: Click the link.
alts: Enter the link.
Enter on the link.
why: You 'click' a link or button. 'Enter' is for typing data or going into a place.

pt: Estou pensando em viajar nas férias.
understandable: I'm thinking to travel in the vacation.
natural: I'm thinking of traveling on vacation.
alts: I'm thinking to travel in the vacations.
I think about to travel on vacation.
why: 'Think of/about' takes a noun or -ing form. 'On vacation' is the fixed expression.

understandable: I live near of my work.
natural: I live close to work.
alts: I live near of the work.
I live next of my job.
why: 'Near' takes no preposition; 'close' takes 'to'. 'Work' as a place has no article: 'at work', 'close to work'.

understandable: I am delayed.
natural: I'm running late.
alts: I'm with delay.
I am delayed for the meeting.
why: 'Delayed' describes things (flights, trains). For yourself, say 'I'm running late' or 'I'm going to be late'.

understandable: I grew with my grandparents.
natural: I grew up with my grandparents.
alts: I raised with my grandparents.
I grew with up my grandparents.
why: 'Grow up' is the phrasal verb for becoming an adult. 'Raise' is something done to someone else.

pt: Preciso descer do ônibus no próximo ponto.
understandable: I need to go down of the bus at the next point.
natural: I need to get off the bus at the next stop.
alts: I need to go out the bus at the next point.
I need to descend the bus at the next stop.
why: Use 'get off' for buses, trains and planes (and 'get on' to board). A bus 'ponto' is a 'stop'.

understandable: It depends of the situation.
natural: It depends on the situation.
alts: It depends from the situation.
It depends about the situation.
why: 'Depend' is always followed by 'on'.

pt: Estou de acordo com a proposta, mas tenho dúvidas.
understandable: I'm in agreement with the proposal, but I have doubts.
natural: I'm on board with the proposal, but I have some reservations.
alts: I'm on agreement with the proposal, but I have some doubts.
I'm of the same agreement with the proposal, but I have doubts.
why: 'On board with' is a natural business idiom, and 'reservations' sounds more professional than 'doubts' when you want to be diplomatic.

understandable: Let's mark a meeting.
natural: Let's schedule a meeting.
alts: Let's make a reunion.
Let's mark up a meeting.
why: You 'schedule' or 'set up' a meeting. 'Reunion' is a gathering of people after years apart.

pt: Eu não tenho nada a ver com isso.
understandable: I have nothing to see with this.
natural: I have nothing to do with this.
alts: I don't have nothing to do with this.
I have nothing of do with this.
why: The idiom is 'have nothing to do with'. Remember English avoids double negatives.

pt: O sistema está fora do ar.
understandable: The system is out of the air.
natural: The system is down.
alts: The system is out of air.
The system fell.
why: A service that is unavailable is 'down'. When it works again it's 'back up'.

understandable: I'm without time right now.
natural: I'm really swamped right now.
alts: I'm very occupied right now.
I have a lot of busy right now.
why: 'Swamped' (or 'tied up', 'slammed') is the natural way to say you have too much work.

understandable: For me it's the same.
natural: I don't mind either way.
alts: To me it does no difference.
For me, it's all equal.
why: 'I don't mind either way' or 'It makes no difference to me' express indifference naturally.

understandable: I was bothered with him.
natural: I was upset with him.
alts: I was annoyed of him.
I stayed angry about him.
why: Use 'upset/annoyed/angry WITH someone' and 'about/at' a situation. 'Stay' doesn't describe an emotional reaction.

pt: O voo foi cancelado e fiquei sem saber o que fazer.
understandable: The flight was cancelled and I stayed without knowing what to do.
natural: The flight was cancelled and I didn't know what to do.
alts: The flight was cancelled and I stayed not knowing what to do.
The flight was cancelled and I was without to know what to do.
why: 'Ficar sem' is rarely translated with 'stay without'. Just use a simple past negative.

understandable: I am inside of the subject.
natural: I'm up to speed on this.
alts: I'm inside the subject.
I'm in the inside of the topic.
why: 'Up to speed' (or 'in the loop') means fully informed about the latest situation.

pt: Não vejo a hora de viajar.
understandable: I don't see the hour to travel.
natural: I can't wait to travel.
alts: I don't see the time to travel.
I'm not waiting to travel.
why: 'I can't wait to + verb' expresses strong excitement about a future event.

pt: Concordo com você até certo ponto.
understandable: I agree with you until a point.
natural: I agree with you up to a point.
alts: I agree you up to a point.
I agree with you at one point.
why: The fixed phrase is 'up to a point' (or 'to some extent'). Agree is followed by 'with' + person.

pt: Preciso de um tempo pra testar isso antes de colocar no ar.
understandable: I need some time to test this before putting it in the air.
natural: I need a bit of time to test this before it goes live.
alts: I need some time to test this before it goes to the air.
I need some time to test this before I put it on live.
why: Software 'goes live' (or 'is deployed') when released to users.

understandable: They cut my vacancy.
natural: I was laid off.
alts: I was fired out.
I was put out of the company.
why: 'Laid off' means losing your job because the company reduced staff. 'Fired' means dismissed for something you did.

understandable: We finished.
natural: We broke up.
alts: We finished our dating.
We have terminated.
why: 'Break up' is the phrasal verb for ending a romantic relationship.

understandable: I just have arrived.
natural: I just got here.
alts: I have just arrive.
I finish to arrive.
why: 'Just' goes before the main verb: 'I just got here' (or 'I've just arrived').

understandable: He gave me a cake.
natural: He stood me up.
alts: He gave me a no-show.
He left me standing out.
why: 'Stand someone up' means to not show up to a date or meeting without warning.

pt: Vou levar isso para o meu gerente.
understandable: I will take this to my superiors.
natural: I'll escalate this to my manager.
alts: I'll go up this with my manager.
I'll take up this to my manager.
why: 'Escalate' is the standard business verb for passing an issue to someone more senior.

understandable: I am not much fan of this.
natural: I'm not a big fan of this.
alts: I'm not very fan of this.
I don't be a fan of this.
why: 'Fan' is a noun, so it needs an article: 'a big fan', 'a huge fan'.

understandable: I'm with my eye on this.
natural: I'm keeping an eye on this.
alts: I have an eye on this.
I'm watching eye on this.
why: 'Keep an eye on' means to monitor something.

understandable: It doesn't worth the pain.
natural: It's not worth it.
alts: It doesn't worth it.
It's not worthy.
why: 'Worth' behaves like a preposition: 'be worth it', 'be worth + noun/-ing'. It is never a main verb with 'do/does'.

pt: Embora ele seja jovem, tem muita experiência.
understandable: Despite he is young, he has much experience.
natural: Although he's young, he has a lot of experience.
alts: In spite he is young, he has a lot of experience.
Even he is young, he has much experience.
why: 'Although' introduces a clause; 'despite' needs a noun or -ing. 'Much' is rare in positive sentences; use 'a lot of'.

understandable: If I would have known, I would have warned you.
natural: If I'd known, I would have told you.
alts: If I would know, I would tell you.
If I knew, I would have told you.
why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Never 'would' in the if-clause.

understandable: I hope that it gives right.
natural: Fingers crossed it works out.
alts: Hopefully it will be right.
I wish it works out.
why: 'Work out' means to end well. 'Fingers crossed' is a friendly, informal way to wish for luck.

pt: Vamos alinhar isso na reunião de amanhã.
understandable: Let's align this in tomorrow's meeting.
natural: Let's get on the same page during tomorrow's meeting.
alts: Let's make an alignment tomorrow.
Let's sync up on that tomorrow.
why: 'Get on the same page' and 'sync up' are the authentic English idioms for aligning expectations.

pt: Vou repassar isso para a equipe depois do almoço.
understandable: I will pass this to the team after lunch.
natural: I'll brief the team right after lunch.
alts: I'll forward this information to the team.
I'll loop the team in after lunch.
why: 'Brief the team' or 'loop someone in' convey professional communication much better than a literal 'pass to'.

pt: Pensando bem, talvez seja melhor adiar.
understandable: Thinking well, maybe it is better to postpone.
natural: On second thought, it might be better to hold off.
alts: Reflecting well, we should wait.
Thinking better, we could wait.
why: 'Pensando bem' translates naturally as 'On second thought'; 'hold off' is natural for waiting before taking action.

pt: No final das contas, o que importa é a satisfação do cliente.
understandable: In the end of the accounts, what matters is client satisfaction.
natural: At the end of the day, customer satisfaction is what really counts.
alts: When all is said and done, customer satisfaction matters most.
Ultimately, customer happiness is key.
why: 'At the end of the day' or 'When all is said and done' is the standard equivalent of 'no final das contas'.

pt: Vou te manter informado sobre qualquer novidade.
understandable: I will maintain you informed about any novelty.
natural: I'll keep you posted on any updates.
alts: I'll keep you in the loop.
I will let you know as soon as things develop.
why: 'Keep someone posted' or 'keep someone in the loop' is much more natural than 'maintain informed'.

pt: Não vale a pena reinventar a roda para resolver isso.
understandable: It doesn't worth to reinvent the wheel for this.
natural: There's no point in reinventing the wheel to solve this.
alts: It makes no sense to reinvent the wheel.
We shouldn't reinvent the wheel.
why: 'There is no point in + -ing' expresses 'não vale a pena / não faz sentido'.

pt: Não me entenda mal, eu gosto do projeto, mas precisamos de ajustes.
understandable: Don't understand me wrong, I like the project.
natural: Don't get me wrong, I like the project, but we need some tweaks.
alts: Don't take this the wrong way, but...
I don't mean to criticize, but...
why: 'Don't get me wrong' or 'Don't take this the wrong way' is the natural way to soften an objection.

pt: Precisamos pesar os prós e os contras antes de assinar.
understandable: We need to weigh the pros and cons before to sign.
natural: We need to weigh the pros and cons before signing.
alts: We should assess the trade-offs before committing.
We need to consider the upsides and downsides.
why: Prepositions (like 'before') are followed by gerund (-ing): 'before signing', not 'before to sign'.

pt: Estou sobrecarregado com tarefas esta semana.
understandable: I am overloaded of tasks this week.
natural: I'm completely swamped with work this week.
alts: I'm up to my ears in deadlines.
I'm overwhelmed by the workload.
why: 'Swamped with' or 'snowed under with' is native, expressive vocabulary for being very busy.

pt: Para encurtar a história, nós conseguimos entregar a tempo.
understandable: To shorten the story, we achieved to deliver on time.
natural: Long story short, we managed to deliver on time.
alts: To cut a long story short, we made the deadline.
In short, we got it delivered on time.
why: 'Long story short' is the classic idiom; 'managed to deliver' translates 'conseguimos entregar' (avoid 'achieved to deliver').

understandable: I completely disagree with you.
natural: I see your point, though I look at it slightly differently.
alts: I understand your view, though I have a different take.
why: In English meetings, softening disagreement keeps the conversation constructive.

understandable: You need to change this today.
natural: Could we prioritize updating this before end of day?
alts: Would it be possible to adjust this today?
why: Requests framed as questions sound collaborative rather than bossy.

understandable: This deadline is impossible.
natural: That timeline feels a bit tight given the testing required.
alts: I am not sure that timeline is realistic with full testing.
why: Flagging constraints calmly sounds far more senior than flatly saying "impossible".

pt: Não entendi o que você falou.
understandable: I did not understand what you said.
natural: Could you clarify what you meant by that last point?
alts: Sorry, could you walk me through that part again?
why: Asking for clarification on a specific point sounds confident and attentive.

pt: Vou te mandar o arquivo depois.
understandable: I will send you the file later.
natural: I will follow up with the file right after our call.
alts: I will share the document with you shortly after we wrap up.
why: "Follow up with" + exact timing sounds crisp and reliable.

pt: Tivemos um grande problema no sistema.
understandable: We had a big problem in the system.
natural: We ran into an unexpected bottleneck in production.
alts: We experienced a brief service disruption this morning.
why: "Run into a bottleneck" or "service disruption" is standard technical/business register.

pt: Me dá um retorno até sexta.
understandable: Give me a return until Friday.
natural: Could you get back to me by Friday?
alts: Let me know your thoughts by Friday, if possible.
why: Never translate "dar um retorno" as "give a return"; use "get back to me" + "by".

understandable: We need to align this subject.
natural: We should get on the same page about the scope.
alts: Let us make sure we are aligned on the scope.
why: Use "aligned on [topic]" or "get on the same page".

understandable: I will assume this task.
natural: I will take ownership of this task.
alts: I can take the lead on this one.
why: "Take ownership of" or "take the lead on" sounds natural for responsibilities.

understandable: This will give a lot of work.
natural: This is going to be fairly labor-intensive.
alts: This will require quite a bit of effort upfront.
why: Avoid "give work" from Portuguese; use "require effort" or "be labor-intensive".

pt: Vamos encerrar a reunião por aqui.
understandable: Let us close the meeting here.
natural: Let us wrap up here and give everyone five minutes back.
alts: I think that covers everything—shall we wrap up?
why: "Wrap up" is the standard natural phrasal verb for ending a meeting.

pt: Qual é a sua opinião sincera?
understandable: What is your sincere opinion?
natural: What is your candid take on this proposal?
alts: Be honest—what are your reservations about this?
why: "Candid take" is much more idiomatic in English business discussions than "sincere opinion".

pt: Você esqueceu de anexar o PDF.
understandable: You forgot to attach the PDF.
natural: It looks like the PDF did not come through—could you resend it?
alts: Just a heads-up, I think the attachment got left off.
why: Blaming the file rather than the person is classic English workplace politeness.

understandable: The meeting was very productive.
natural: We made solid headway in today's session.
alts: That was a really constructive discussion.
why: "Make headway" or "constructive discussion" elevates B1 phrasing to B2+.

understandable: I agree in parts.
natural: I partly agree, though I have one concern.
alts: I am on board with most of this, except for one detail.
why: Never say "in parts"; say "partly agree" or "agree to some extent".

understandable: Let us focus on what matters.
natural: Let us zero in on the highest-impact items first.
alts: To keep us focused, let us prioritize the top two issues.
why: "Zero in on" is a natural B2+ phrasal verb for focusing sharply.

pt: Isso não faz parte do meu escopo.
understandable: This is not part of my scope.
natural: That falls outside the current scope of this sprint.
alts: We did not factor that into the current scope.
why: "Fall outside the scope" is the natural collocation.

understandable: We need to think outside the box.
natural: We may need a less conventional approach here.
alts: Let us step back and look at this from a fresh angle.
why: Replacing overused clichés like "outside the box" sounds sharper and more C1.

understandable: Sorry for the delay to answer.
natural: Thanks for your patience—here is the update you asked for.
alts: Apologies for the delayed reply.
why: "Thanks for your patience" or "Apologies for the delayed reply" beats "delay to answer".

pt: A decisão ainda está em aberto.
understandable: The decision is still open.
natural: The final call is still up in the air.
alts: We have not finalized that decision yet.
why: "Up in the air" is an everyday business idiom for undecided.

pt: Vou verificar com o meu time.
understandable: I will verify with my team.
natural: Let me double-check with the team and circle back.
alts: I will confirm with my team and let you know.
why: "Check with" and "circle back" are much more natural in calls than "verify with".

understandable: The client complained of the price.
natural: The client pushed back on pricing during the call.
alts: The client raised concerns about the cost.
why: "Push back on" or "raise concerns about" fits business negotiations.

understandable: We have to solve this urgent.
natural: We need to address this as a top priority.
alts: This needs immediate attention before anything else.
why: Never use adjective "urgent" as an adverb; use "urgently" or "as a top priority".

pt: Em resumo, o projeto deu certo.
understandable: In summary, the project went right.
natural: Overall, the rollout exceeded our initial targets.
alts: To sum up, the launch was a clear success.
why: "Exceeded targets" or "was a clear success" sounds natural rather than "went right".

understandable: Actually, I live in São Paulo.
natural: Currently, I live in São Paulo.
alts: Right now, I live in São Paulo.
why: False friend: "actually" means "na verdade"; for "atualmente", use "currently" or "right now".

understandable: I pretend to travel on vacation.
natural: I plan to travel during my vacation.
alts: I intend to travel on vacation.
why: False friend: "pretend" means "fingir"! Use "plan to" or "intend to".

understandable: You need to push the door.
natural: You need to pull the door.
alts: Pull the door toward you.
why: Classic trap: "push" = empurrar; "pull" = puxar.

pt: Vou visitar meus parentes no domingo.
understandable: I will visit my parents on Sunday.
natural: I am going to visit my relatives on Sunday.
alts: I am visiting extended family on Sunday.
why: "Parents" = pai e mãe; for aunts, uncles, and cousins, use "relatives".

pt: Eu fiz uma pergunta para ele.
understandable: I made a question for him.
natural: I asked him a question.
alts: I had a question for him.
why: Never "make a question"; always "ask someone a question".

understandable: I will cut my hair tomorrow.
natural: I am going to get a haircut tomorrow.
alts: I am getting my hair cut tomorrow.
why: Saying "I will cut my hair" sounds like you are using scissors yourself!

pt: Vamos decidir na hora conforme for acontecendo.
understandable: Let us decide on the hour as it happens.
natural: Let us play it by ear.
alts: Let us see how things go and adjust on the fly.
why: "Play it by ear" is the exact natural idiom for deciding flexibly as things unfold.

understandable: For today it is enough, let us close.
natural: Let us call it a day.
alts: That is a wrap for today.
why: "Call it a day" is everyday natural English for stopping work for the day.

understandable: They saved money cutting important steps.
natural: They cut corners on testing to ship faster.
alts: They took shortcuts that hurt quality.
why: "Cut corners" means skipping essential steps to save time or money.

pt: Ela começou no novo emprego já entregando resultado rápido.
understandable: She started the new job already delivering fast results.
natural: She hit the ground running in her new role.
alts: She got up to speed remarkably fast.
why: "Hit the ground running" means starting a new job or project with immediate energy and results.

understandable: I am a bit indisposed today.
natural: I am feeling a bit under the weather today.
alts: I am not feeling 100% today.
why: "Under the weather" is the natural everyday way to say you feel slightly sick.

pt: Precisamos quebrar o gelo antes de negociar.
understandable: We need to break the ice before negotiating.
natural: Let us break the ice with a quick round of introductions.
alts: Let us start with some light small talk to break the ice.
why: "Break the ice" works identically in English—pair it with "small talk" or "introductions".

pt: Ainda estou tentando entender essa arquitetura nova.
understandable: I am still trying to understand this new architecture.
natural: I am still trying to wrap my head around this new architecture.
alts: It is taking me a moment to get my head around this design.
why: "Wrap your head around something" is super common for understanding complex ideas.

pt: Ele perdeu o prazo e deixou a tarefa escapar.
understandable: He lost the deadline and let the task escape.
natural: He missed the deadline and the task fell through the cracks.
alts: The follow-up slipped through the cracks.
why: Use "miss a deadline" (never "lose a deadline") and "fall through the cracks".

pt: A comida estava muito gostosa, comi demais.
understandable: The food was very tasty, I ate too much.
natural: The food was delicious—I am completely stuffed!
alts: That was amazing; I couldn't eat another bite.
why: "I am stuffed" is natural spoken English after a big meal (avoid "I am full" if you want variety, though both work; never "I am pregnant"!).

pt: Vamos manter todo mundo informado para ninguém se perder.
understandable: Let us keep everyone informed so nobody gets lost.
natural: Let us keep everyone in the loop as things move forward.
alts: Make sure we keep all stakeholders in the loop.
why: "Keep someone in the loop" is one of the highest-frequency business idioms in English.
